author: GamingBolt
description:
Gears of War: E-Day has a pretty damn great all-around multiplayer suite. There are, of course, still objective shortcomings and problems: the PvP modes lack a lot of maps, for example, and as much as I like Horde Siege, I do miss classic Horde – and that’s simply not available in the game, nor is it clear if it is planned to be added via post-launch updates either. 

Like I said previously, too, there are enough changes made to the flow of a game, and classic Gears was unique enough, that I can imagine at least some fans of the older games feeling disappointed or underwhelmed at all the changes. 

But, equally, as I said, most long time fans will find themselves coming around to the changes, if they give themselves the opportunity to keep an open mind. Whether it’s the PvP side of multiplayer that you enjoy, or the horde mode side, Gears E-Day’s multiplayer mode is going to provide countless hours of entertainment to fans new and old alike.
title: Gears of War: E-Day Multiplayer Review - A Pretty Damn Great All-Around Multiplayer Suite

author: GamingBolt
description:
As well as it lends itself to high-speed thrills in surprising ways, the Star Wars franchise hasn’t been terribly active in the racing genre with its video game outings over the years. And yet it still manages to knock the ball out of the part with Star Wars: Galactic Racer with shocking confidence. 

Combining the Star Wars universe with the arcadey action and adrenaline-fueled thrills of a typical Burnout game, Galactic Racer delivers one of the best and most surprising arcade racing experiences in recent memory. Naturally, many will be diving into its offerings in the near future to get a taste of those offerings, and to help you do just that, here, we’ve compiled a list of handy pointers that should aid you in getting to grips with the game much faster. Without further ado then, let’s get started.
title: 15 Things Star Wars: Galatic Racer Doesn't Tell You

author: GamingBolt
description:
In case you haven't heard, I'm rather...obsessed with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, especially after the free Remastered update. Even with its issues, it brings a more contemporary look, and its many new gameplay additions bring it in line with some of the best the genre has to offer. Of course, that only raises the question: How exactly does it compare to the very best open-world games of yesteryear?

We've already seen how Geralt's journey matches up against Crimson Desert, especially with the latter receiving its own massive Enhanced update. But what about CD Projekt RED's own Cyberpunk 2077? Red Dead Redemption 2? The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom? Ghost of Tsushima? Elden Ring? Or better yet, all of them?
title: The Witcher 3 Remastered: How Far Ahead Or Behind Is It Today?
